latin.479: Tu prius probas, nimirum, per peccatum quod in mundum introiit intelligendum esse primum peccatum actuale Adami, sed addis (quod tuam mentem obscurat) id peccatum in nos transfusum originale dici: Et mox, peccatum originale in nobis ex illo esse: Item, Adamum in nos corruptionem genitura transfudisse, quam peccatum originale dicimus. Et paulo post, hoc peccatum ab ipso quidem Adamo commissum esse, sed culpa atque reatu per imputationem in nos transiisse, Ideoque in ipso actuale & personale fuisse, sed in nobis originale dici. Sic modo peccatum originale cum peccato actuali Adami confundis modo distinguis, & modo peccatum actuale Adami cum corruptione originaria commisces; modo ab ea separas.
latin.480: Loquere, te rogo & quaeso, distinctius & magis enucleate: nihil enim adeo veritatis indagationi officit, ac vel ambiguitas orationis, vel ejus cui tecum res est inconstantia & lubricitas sermonis. Si, quod nonnulli faciunt, duo credis peccata originalia, unum imputatum, alterum nobis inhaerens, cur nullo loco id dicis aperte? Si non nisi unum credis, dic constanter, aut cum Pighio id esse peccatum actuale Adami nobis omnibus imputatum, aut cum fidei confessione nostrarum Ecclesiarum corruptionem haereditariam, seu vitium inhaerens: nec duo ista permisce aut contunde, quae secundum tuam sententiam maximo intervallo inter se distant.
latin.481: Peccatum primum actuale Adami ante quinque millia annorum commissum praeteriit, nec permansit in rerum natura: vitium inhaerens cum natura humana permansit, estque & viget hodie. Illud unicum est numero, hujus tot sunt individua quot homines. Illud fuit actio, hoc se habet ad modum habitus. Illud extra nos est, nec possibile est esse in nobis, hoc est intra nos in nobis haerens. Illud tu putas nostrum esse, sed imputatione duntaxat Dei, hoc vere nostrum est, nobis penitus inhaerens: Illud vis esse culpam, hoc illius poenam. Hac ambiguitate & confusione sublata, videamus quibus rationibus probes, Apostolum per peccatum quod in mundum introiit peccatum actuale Adami intelligere. Quae certe fuit sententia Pighii, quam ipse Bellarminus aliquot argumentis confutavit, sed nolo te praejudiciis urgere.
latin.482: Uteris, quantum colligere possum, quatuor argumentis. 1. Per unum hominem Apostolus intelligit primum hominem scilicet Adamum. Ergo per peccatum quod per unum hominem introiit in Mundum intelligit primum peccatum actuale Adami. Nego sequi. Non enim Apostolus dicit Adami peccatum, sed per Adamum peccatum introiisse in Mundum. Adamum considerat ut huius peccati causam, Mundum, id est, homines ut subiectum: nec docere voluit, quis primus in Mundo peccaverit (nam Adamo prior Eva, & hac prior diabolus peccavit) sed in omnes homines per Adamum introductam esse corruptionem peccati.
latin.483: 2. Apostolus agit de peccato quod Mundum infecit, & mortem invexit. Hoc autem convenit tantum peccato actuali Adami ex quo peccatum originale in nobis. Ergo Apostolus agit tantum de peccato actuali Adami. Distinguo peccatum quod Mundum infecit: nam infecisse dicitur vel formaliter, vel causaliter sive efficienter. Priori modo mundum infecit vitium & corruptio inhaerens, posteriore peccatum actuale Adami. Loquitur autem Apostolus hoc versu de peccato quod infecit mundum priori modo: non enim ait peccatum infecisse mundum, sed introisse in mundum. Peccatum actuale Adami mundum infecisse dicitur causaliter, quia causa est ejus peccati quod introiit in mundum. Peccatum vero quod introiit in mundum, cum sit intra mundum formaliter eum afficit & inficit in quo est.
latin.484: 3. ἡ ἁμαρτία cum articulo certum peccati individuum designat, adeo quidem ut vix apud Paulum invenias τὴν ἁμαρτίαν addito articulo aliud declarare, ut notant doctissimi interpretes. Ergo non designat corruptionem haereditariam, quae non est unum peccati individuum, sed peccatum actuale Adami. Nego antecedens. Nullum interpretem me legere memini, qui nomen ἁμαρτία cum praefixo articulo observet certum peccati individuum seu singulare quoddam peccatum unum numero apud Paulum significare: contra observant id fere ubique haereditariam illam corruptionem, quae in omnibus hominibus inest ab ortu, designare. Quarta denique tua ratio est petita ex aliis nominibus, quibus tu putas Apostolum hoc peccatum quod in mundum introiit insignivisse. Quod in sequentibus versibus Apostolus vocat παράβασιν transgressionem, παράπτωμα lapsum seu defectionem, παρακοήν inobedientiam, illud est peccatum actuale Adami. Atqui hoc peccatum quod in mundum introiit, vocat Apostolus παράβασιν, παράπτωμα, & παρακοήν. Ergo hoc peccatum, quod in mundum introiit, est peccatum actuale Adami.

pass_a.479: The first member you grant—entered-sin = Adam's first actual—then cloud it: that same act, poured into us, is styled original; soon original in us is from it; Adam by generation poured a corruption we name original sin; a little later the deed was Adam's own, yet by guilt and reatus it crossed by imputation, actual and personal in him, original only in us. So you fuse original with his actual, then split them; fuse his actual with origin's corruption, then peel them apart.
pass_a.480: I beg a clearer tongue. Ambiguous or slippery speech kills inquiry faster than almost anything. If with some you hold two originals—one imputed, one inhering—say so in plain words somewhere. If only one, hold the line: either Pighius (Adam's actual reckoned to all) or our churches' confession (hereditary corruption / inhering vice). Do not mash together what, on your own showing, stand at the widest remove.
pass_a.481: Five millennia back Adam's first deed of sin is gone from the furniture of things; the vice that sticks with human nature is still alive and at work. One act then; as many inhering instances now as there are persons. Deed versus habit-shape; outside us and impossible to lodge in us versus inside and clinging; ours only if God reckons it versus ours because it truly inheres; fault on your telling versus penalty of that fault. Clear that fog, and ask what reasons force Romans 5's entered-sin to mean Adam's actual—Pighius's line, which even Bellarmine answered with several strokes. I will not blunt you with those prejudices here.
pass_a.482: Four strokes, so far as I can count them. First: 'one man' means Adam the first; therefore the sin that entered through one man is Adam's first actual. The consequence fails. Paul never writes 'Adam's sin' here; he writes that through Adam sin entered the World. Adam is cast as cause, the World (humans) as subject. He is not ranking who first sinned on earth—Eve before Adam, the devil before Eve—but teaching that through Adam sin's corruption was brought in upon all.
pass_a.483: Second: Paul speaks of the sin that infected the World and ushered death; only Adam's actual, the fountain of our original, fits that; therefore only that actual is in view. Distinguish infection: formal versus causal (efficient). Formally, inhering vice and corruption infect; causally, Adam's actual does. This verse uses the former register—he says entered into the world, not infected it. Causal infection belongs to Adam's actual as cause of the entered sin; the entered sin, being inside the world, formally touches and infects what holds it.
pass_a.484: Third: the articular he hamartia marks one numbered sin-instance—so rarely anything else in Paul, the learned say—hence not hereditary corruption (many instances) but Adam's actual. Antecedent denied: I know no reader who takes articular hamartia in Paul as one singular numbered deed; rather they take it almost everywhere for the birth-corruption in every human. Fourth stroke: later names—parabasis, paraptoma, parakoe—mark Adam's actual; and the entered-sin bears those same names; therefore the entered-sin is that actual. Tip here before Placeus pries the names apart.

479: You prove the prior, namely that by the sin which entered into the world Adam's first actual sin must be understood, but you add (which obscures your mind) that that sin transfused into us is called original: And soon, that original sin in us is from it: Likewise, that Adam by begetting transfused into us a corruption which we call original sin. And a little later, that this sin was indeed committed by Adam himself, but that by guilt and reatus it passed into us by imputation, And so in him was actual and personal, but in us is called original. Thus you sometimes confuse original sin with Adam's actual sin, sometimes distinguish, and sometimes mix Adam's actual sin with origin's corruption; sometimes you separate it from it.
480: Speak, I beg and ask you, more distinctly and more clearly: for nothing so hinders the investigation of truth as either ambiguity of speech, or the inconstancy and slipperiness of speech of the one with whom you have to do. If, as some do, you believe two original sins, one imputed, the other inhering in us, why nowhere do you say that openly? If you believe only one, say constantly, either with Pighius that it is Adam's actual sin imputed to us all, or with the confession of faith of our Churches that it is hereditary corruption, or inhering vice: and do not mix or crush those two which according to your opinion stand a maximum interval apart from each other.
481: Adam's first actual sin, committed some five thousand years ago, has passed, and did not remain in the nature of things: inhering vice remained with human nature, and is and thrives today. That is unique in number; of this there are as many individuals as there are humans. That was an action; this stands in the manner of a habit. That is outside us, and it is not possible for it to be in us; this is within us, sticking in us. That you think is ours, but only by God's imputation; this is truly ours, deeply inhering in us: That you will have as fault; this as its penalty. With this ambiguity and confusion removed, let us see by what reasons you prove that the Apostle by the sin which entered into the world understands Adam's actual sin. Which was certainly Pighius's opinion, which Bellarmine himself refuted with some arguments, but I do not wish to press you with prejudices.
482: You use, as far as I can gather, four arguments. 1. By one man the Apostle understands the first man, namely Adam. Therefore by the sin which entered into the World through one man he understands Adam's first actual sin. I deny that it follows. For the Apostle does not say Adam's sin, but that through Adam sin entered into the World. He considers Adam as the cause of this sin, the World—that is, humans—as the subject: nor did he wish to teach who first sinned in the World (for Eve before Adam, and before her the devil, sinned) but that through Adam the corruption of sin was introduced into all humans.
483: 2. The Apostle treats of the sin which infected the World and brought in death. But this fits only Adam's actual sin from which original sin is in us. Therefore the Apostle treats only of Adam's actual sin. I distinguish the sin which infected the World: for it is said to have infected either formally, or causally or efficiently. In the former way inhering vice and corruption infected the world; in the latter Adam's actual sin. But the Apostle in this verse speaks of the sin which infected the world in the former way: for he does not say that sin infected the world, but that it entered into the world. Adam's actual sin is said to have infected the world causally, because it is the cause of that sin which entered into the world. But the sin which entered into the world, since it is inside the world, formally affects and infects that in which it is.
484: 3. He hamartia with the article designates a certain individual of sin, so much so that scarcely in Paul do you find ten hamartian with the article added declaring anything else, as the most learned interpreters note. Therefore it does not designate hereditary corruption, which is not one individual of sin, but Adam's actual sin. I deny the antecedent. I remember reading no interpreter who observes that the name hamartia with the prefixed article signifies among Paul a certain individual of sin or some singular sin one in number: on the contrary they observe that almost everywhere it designates that hereditary corruption which is in all humans from birth. Your fourth reason finally is sought from other names by which you think the Apostle marked this sin which entered into the world. What in the following verses the Apostle calls parabasis, transgression, paraptoma, a fall or defection, parakoe, disobedience—that is Adam's actual sin. But this sin which entered into the world the Apostle calls parabasis, paraptoma, and parakoe. Therefore this sin which entered into the world is Adam's actual sin.
